entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Severe - the complete lack sounds like deprivation, emptiness that hurts.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and absolute, naming total emptiness while passing no verdict on it.
examples: the sentence was devoid of meaning

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The approving member - the same complete lack is a relief, the absent thing one you are better off without.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Light and wry - complete absence made to sound blameless, the opposite colouring to *destitute*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Registers the nonexistence as a deficiency rather than a bare fact, which *absent* does not.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Points at the gap - the nonexistence is felt as a hole where something belonged.

entries.definition: not having existence or being or actuality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and absolute - the thing simply has no being, without the sense in *missing* that it was expected somewhere.

entries.definition: no longer existing or inaccessible through loss or destruction
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and dry - marks the thing as gone through loss or destruction and judges nothing about it.
examples: its nonextant original was written on vellum

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries the drama of a disappearance - existence not merely denied but ended, where *nonexistent* implies no before.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most judging of these - the nonexistence reads as falling short of a mark, not merely as nothing being there.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Steps up from *expensive* to a price high enough to be remarkable, still with no verdict attached to it.
examples: big-ticket items like cars and furs

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Weightier than *high-priced*, the price felt as a cost borne rather than a number quoted.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: British, and softer than *costly* — the same high price delivered in an everyday, conversational word.
examples: much too dear for my pocketbook

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Moves the price off money entirely onto loss or sacrifice, naming what something took without condemning it.

entries.definition: high in price or charging high prices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain word for a high price, stating the fact without deciding whether the price is deserved.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and purely descriptive: it says the price is high and refuses any attitude toward it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries the same very-high price as *big-ticket* in a flatter, more transactional ring.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Judgement rather than measurement — it sets the price against the value and finds it unearned.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and faintly grumbling — the high price registered as a small complaint rather than a measurement.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same informal grumble as *pricey* in a clipped spelling, with no shift in force.

entries.definition: of laws and regulations; designed to protect trade and commerce from unfair business practices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely classificatory - it says what a law or regulation is built to protect trade from, and commends no one.

entries.definition: of laws and regulations; designed to protect trade and commerce from unfair business practices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and as neutral as *antimonopoly*, marking a regulation's protective purpose rather than approving anybody's conduct.

entries.definition: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approves by negation - nothing foul in the play - where *sportsmanlike* names the virtue outright.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The emphatic one - its doubled phrasing insists there is nothing left to question, where *just* simply states that the standard was met.

entries.definition: of a person; just and impartial; not prejudiced
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises a settled cast of mind rather than a single dealing - the impartiality is lodged in the person.

entries.definition: free from favoritism or self-interest or bias or deception; conforming with established standards or rules
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain, unarguable approval - it certifies that no favoritism or deception got in, without the weight of principle *just* carries.

entries.definition: free from favoritism or self-interest or bias or deception; conforming with established standards or rules
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Heavier than *fair* - the same absence of bias, but weighted as a standard rightly upheld rather than a condition merely met.

entries.definition: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmer and easier than *clean*, crediting fair play as a spirit brought to the contest rather than a rule left unbroken.
examples: a sporting solution of the disagreement

entries.definition: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The formal member - it measures conduct against a named standard of sportsmanship instead of merely reporting, as *clean* does, that nothing foul happened.

entries.definition: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most casual of these, informal and light, granting the same approval with none of *sportsmanlike*'s weight.
examples: a sporting solution of the disagreement

entries.definition: having more than the average number of accidents
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mildly damning - it turns a count of mishaps into a standing property of whatever it is aimed at, so the accidents read as owed to it rather than to chance.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral but predictive - it treats the leaning as a matter of the subject's nature, so what follows sounds expected rather than merely possible.
examples: he is apt to ignore matters he considers unimportant

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and dry - the leaning sounds like a settled arrangement of temperament rather than an appetite, cooler than *given*.

entries.definition: (followed by ‘of’ or ‘to’) having a strong preference or liking for
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Warm - the leaning is felt as liking rather than as mere direction, which is what lifts it clear of *inclined*.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Blunt and settled - the disposition sounds ingrained rather than merely present, heavier and more everyday than *disposed*.

entries.definition: (often followed by ‘to’) having a preference, disposition, or tendency
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Mild and non-committal - the leaning is stated lightly enough to leave room for doing otherwise, where *prone* fixes it in place.
examples: wasn't inclined to believe the excuse

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the disposition in the subject's cast of mind rather than in what it does, which is what separates it from *tending*.
examples: I am not minded to answer any questions

entries.definition: (followed by ‘of’ or ‘to’) having a strong preference or liking for
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Lighter and more indulgent than *fond* - it casts the strong liking as a weakness cheerfully admitted.

entries.definition: having a tendency (to); often used in combination
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and fixing - it states the tendency as a standing liability rather than a leaning, and welds straight onto whatever is tended toward.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest of these - it names the direction of the leaning and claims nothing about temperament or liking.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The barest approval here - it grants appeal to the mind without characterizing that appeal at all.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Makes the cultivation conspicuous, so the compliment carries an edge *intellectual* does not.
examples: highbrow events such as the ballet or opera

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same claim to high cultivation as *highbrow*, but the participial form sits heavier and stiffer.

entries.definition: appealing to or using the intellect
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain term of the family - it names the faculty being engaged and passes no verdict on it.
examples: intellectual workers engaged in creative literary or artistic or scientific labor
has tremendous intellectual sympathy for oppressed people

entries.definition: having its source in or being guided by the intellect (as distinguished from experience or emotion)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Positional rather than approving - it places the source of the thinking in the intellect as against experience.

entries.definition: devoted to matters of the mind
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Quieter and warmer than *intellectual* - a mind given over to its own concerns rather than one showing power.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Weightier than *good* for the same appeal to the mind, casting it as demanding rather than merely worth having.
